note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 by an independent auditor against Section 3: "MUST NOT drop (as part of GTSM processing) packets classified as Trusted or Unknown." Ze has three GTSM processing points, and each now carries a 3-4 tag with a recorded break. Socket floor: TestGTSMFloorDeliversATrustedPacket (Trusted) and TestGTSMNoFloorDeliversAnUnknownPacket (Unknown), revert records on setIPMinTTL. ICMP-error terms: TestGTSMDeliversAnICMPErrorNoSessionClaims (Unknown errors delivered, no term counter), revert record on quotedIPv4HeaderGuard. Listen-port rule: TestGTSMListenerUnknownNotDropped (Unknown SYNs at TTL/hop limit 1 answered, no counter; mutant on listenPortTerm's MatchSourceAddress) and, new, TestGTSMListenerSYNAtFloorAccepted and its IPv6 twin (listenerAtFloorProof): a SYN from the GTSM peer at TTL/hop limit 255 with floor 255 gets a SYN-ACK, the injected ACK completes a connection the listener accepts from the peer's address, and assertNoTermMatched finds no ze_gtsm counter nonzero; mutant records lower_linux.go:947 lowerIPv4TTLBelowMatch and :972 lowerIPv6HopLimitBelowMatch CmpOpLt->CmpOpLte, observed red. This discharges the previous finding (Trusted half of the listen-port rule tagged only under 3-7). Each claim states what its body checks: at floor 255 the Trusted range is exactly TTL 255, so 'drops no SYN classified Trusted' is not wider than the body. Residuals, not verdict changes: only floor 255 is driven, so a compare of the form ttl != floor would pass at this floor (the claims do not claim other floors); Trusted ICMP errors at TTL 255 are asserted by TestGTSMDeliversAQuotedICMPErrorAtTTL255 under the 3-2 tag, and their only drop path is the same shared lowerIPv4TTLBelowMatch compare the IPv4 at-floor record discriminates; listenerAtFloorProof does not itself read that the listen rule is installed, which the mutant record covers for the recorded run.
